title: Ethernet MAC frame
summary: An Ethernet II (DIX) frame: 6-byte destination MAC, 6-byte source MAC, 2-byte EtherType (or length for 802.3), payload (46-1500 bytes), and 4-byte FCS (CRC-32). Minimum frame (without FCS) is 64 bytes; maximum is 1518 (1522 with 802.1Q VLAN tag).

ext.summary: An Ethernet II (DIX) frame: 6-byte destination MAC, 6-byte source MAC, 2-byte EtherType (or length for 802.3), payload (46-1500 bytes), and 4-byte FCS (CRC-32). Minimum frame (without FCS) is 64 bytes; maximum is 1518 (1522 with 802.1Q VLAN tag).

structure.meaning: Target MAC address (or broadcast FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF, or multicast).
Payload protocol: 0x0800 IPv4, 0x0806 ARP, 0x86DD IPv6, 0x8100 VLAN (802.1Q), 0x88CC LLDP, 0x8906 FCoE. Values ≥ 0x0600 = EtherType; < 0x0600 = 802.3 length.
Upper-layer data. Padded to 46 bytes minimum (to ensure 64-byte minimum frame).
CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) over dst+src+type+payload. Computed by NIC.
TPID 0x8100 + PCP (3 bits) + DEI (1 bit) + VID (12 bits). Inserted between src and EtherType.
Extended payload (up to 9000 bytes) for high-throughput networks. Not standardized but widely supported.

ext.example_hex: ff ff ff ff ff ff 00 11 22 33 44 55 08 00
ext.example_decoded: Ethernet frame: broadcast dst, src 00:11:22:33:44:55, EtherType 0x0800 (IPv4)
notes: Minimum frame is 64 bytes (to detect collisions in half-duplex).
Maximum frame is 1518 bytes (1522 with VLAN).
Jumbo frames (up to 9000 bytes) reduce per-packet overhead for bulk transfer.
Ethernet is the dominant LAN technology (IEEE 802.3).
